references.text: In [ref:Matt 24:40|Matthew 24:40], we find the closely parallel text: "Then two men will be in the field; one is taken and the other left behind." This is Matthew's parallel to Luke 17:36 and describes the same scenario of two people working in the field at the Lord's coming.

The preceding verse [ref:Luk 17:35|Luke 17:35] describes two women grinding grain together—one is taken, the other left behind. Luke 17:36 continues this pattern with two people in the field, illustrating the sudden separation at the coming of the Son of Man.

[ref:Luk 17:34|Luke 17:34] introduces the series of examples: "That night two will be lying in one bed; one will be taken and the other left behind." Verse 36 repeats this same pattern in a different setting—out in the field.

[ref:Luk 17:30|Luke 17:30] provides the context for this separation: "So it will also be on the day when the Son of Man is revealed." Verse 36 illustrates the sudden and unexpected nature of this revelation.

[ref:Matt 24:38-39|Matthew 24:38–39] describes how people were going about their daily lives—eating, drinking, marrying—right up until the flood came and took them all away. The work in the field mentioned in Luke 17:36 represents exactly this ordinary life that is suddenly interrupted at the Lord's coming.

[ref:1 Tess 5:2-3|1 Thessalonians 5:2–3] emphasizes the suddenness of the Lord's day: "The day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night." Luke 17:36 illustrates precisely this suddenness—midway through daily work in the field, one is taken and the other left behind.
